items.summary: A study by Convovo, led by Cornell professor Tapan Parikh, found that when forced to name a candidate for the upcoming midterms via API, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended Republicans about 92% of the time and OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked Democrats in about 97%. Across nearly 500 races, the models agreed less than 10% of the time. Parikh said the lean appears baked into each model — Grok leans through its search terms and sources, while GPT has mostly decided already. The study comes weeks before November 3.
items.title: Study Finds Grok Leans Republican, GPT-Lean Democrat in Midterm Picks

items.summary: Jack Dorsey’s Block released a new voice model called Dessa from its research lab, which runs locally and sounds human with expressions like laughs, pauses, and cries. The company said the model is trained fully on human speech using a single NVIDIA GPU and can talk and listen at once. There is no public access yet, but Block has invited safety researchers to test it.
items.title: Block Releases Human-Sounding Voice Model Named Dessa From Its Research Lab

items.summary: Kaspersky researchers analyzed a new UEFI bootkit named BlackX, deployed in an early-2026 espionage campaign attributed with medium confidence to APT41. It exploited the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to bypass Secure Boot and load malicious drivers targeting diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan. BlackX resembles BlackLotus but deploys different payloads; victims used fully patched Windows 11 systems that remained compromised because administrators did not manually activate additional certificate revocations required by the patch.
items.title: BlackX UEFI Bootkit Exploits Baton Drop Flaw in Central Asia Campaign

items.summary: On 24th October 2026, the author announced adding four-player online mode to Battledrones, where earlier maps supported only two players. Claude Opus 5.5 created a new map called Compass Rose with rotational symmetry for up to four AI or human players joining via share links or QR codes. New teams use purple and green robots alongside existing blue and red designs.
items.title: Author Adds Four-Player Online Mode and Compass Rose Map to Battledrones

items.summary: The author of Ahead of AI announces a new eight-video course, totaling about 11 hours of content, that teaches building reasoning models from scratch. The videos implement methods in Python and PyTorch starting from a pre-trained Qwen3 model to focus on evaluation, inference-time scaling, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, and distillation. The author recommends comfort with Python and PyTorch as prerequisites, notes the earlier Build A Large Language Model course is recommended but not required, and suggests using a GPU for later training experiments while early examples can run on a CPU. Accompanying lectures were recorded over recent months; the companion book Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch) is available from Manning and Amazon in print color edition. The author also recommends an optional LinkedIn Learning course of about 90 minutes as a conceptual preview, plans to return with more LLM research articles next month after a short break, and encourages viewers to pause and try small experiments while watching.
items.title: Author Shares Full Video Course on Building Reasoning Models From Scratch

items.summary: Endurance Energy, a Seattle-based startup, announced it completed the first full operations cycle from drilling to electricity generation at an underwater geothermal plant on an active volcano. The demonstration produced net-positive energy for less than 10 seconds, though founder and CEO Andrew Redd called its implications significant. He said the test confirmed what works at depth and how to build a larger system. Endurance’s next milestone is deploying up to six 2 MW commercial generators in Tonga. Stanford professor Roland Horne noted underwater geothermal may be technically feasible but likely more expensive than on-land models.
items.title: Seattle Startup Completes First Undersea Volcano Power Test

items.summary: The Trump administration has filed a motion in an ongoing federal lawsuit seeking the right to rescind its three-year-old approval of Connecticut’s first offshore wind project, Revolution Wind. The Department of the Interior (DoI) argues remand is warranted so it can reevaluate compliance with the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act and criticise the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management’s 2023 record of decision for failing to “adequately explain” impacts on fishing and recreation. The $6.2 billion, 704-MW project has delivered power since March and is expected to be fully operational by year-end, supplying around 350,000 homes. Ørsted has not commented. DoI says it is complying with a briefing schedule, not changing policy. Critics warn the move injects uncertainty into a nearly completed project that is almost 95 per cent complete and could deter future investment in U.S. renewable energy.
items.title: Trump Administration Files Motion to Rescind Approval of Revolution Wind

items.summary: Iran's oil conflict is pushing up prices across goods, including new cars, which the article says gives cheaper Chinese electric vehicles an edge over struggling Western brands. Protectionist measures limit imports of new Chinese battery-electric vehicles, with tariffs as high as 45. 3% in the EU, while used EVs avoid those duties and price tags up to 40% below MSRP. According to data from China EV Marketplace (CEVM), pre-owned sales to European customers grew 280% year over year, reaching 7,900 units through September. CEVM's COO Jakub Geršl told CarNewsChina that tariffs have weakened demand for new Chinese BEVs and expects a hybrid import cap to pressure plug-in hybrid sales too; the company claims its prices run about 40% below original price on average. The piece notes this trend may accelerate electrification in emerging markets, possibly by 2035, though it frames these as forecasts rather than confirmed outcomes.
items.title: Rising Costs Open Western Markets to Used Chinese EVs

items.summary: Giulia Muia, a renewable energy consultant in Italy, argues that the energy sector must become more inclusive to build resilient systems. She says gender diversity is part of resilience, noting that different people ask different questions—such as when a local farmer reveals land floods—that can save projects. As a leader she asks junior staff first, gives extra time to non-native speakers and shares responsibility with light oversight. Drawing on advice from her former manager at ZE Energy, she encourages young women not to wait until they feel ready, prepare well, engage in the field, seek leaders who listen, and open the door for the woman coming next.
items.title: Solar Leader on Building Inclusive Energy Teams Through Listening and Space

items.summary: The European Sunrise consortium is developing glass-free photovoltaic modules by integrating solar cells directly into fiber-reinforced polymer composites. The approach aims to produce lightweight modules that conform to curved surfaces, expanding applications in vehicle-integrated photovoltaics (VIPV), noise barriers and maritime use. Laboratory tests have shown reflection reductions of up to 50%. Set to run for 36 months until May 2029, the project involves 12 partners from eight countries across three pilot facilities. Partners target weight reduction of at least 80% in VIPV applications, with cost and lamination time savings also sought.
items.title: European consortium develops glass-free photovoltaic modules for vehicles, noise barriers and boats

items.summary: The Zayed Sustainability Prize announced its finalists for the 2027 edition after making final cuts from a record 10,233 submissions across 177 countries. The organization described this as the most competitive cycle in its history and noted that every finalist will now receive guaranteed financial support beyond just winners. Organisational finalists get US $100,000 each while Global High Schools finalists receive US $25,000 each. Finalists span categories including Health, Food, Energy, Water, Climate Action, and Global High Schools. The article then lists brief descriptions of this year's finalists across all six regions before noting that winners will be announced at the awards ceremony on 12 January 2027.
items.title: Zayed Sustainability Prize Names Finalists After Record Submissions

items.summary: The author argues that energy-transition analysis often carries today’s market size into the future, inflating the replacement problem by treating incumbent supply as fixed. Discussing shipping with Amy Rennison at an Earth Set event at Octopus Energy’s London headquarters, he notes roughly 40% of maritime freight tonnage is coal, oil and gas, with iron ore another 15%, while electrification may shrink fuel demand to about 70 million tonnes by 2100 in his projection. He says other projections reach several hundred million tonnes, changing how much biomass, synthetic fuel and infrastructure appear necessary. Ocean physicist Helen Czerski challenged his aviation treatment; he estimates roughly 91% of aviation is discretionary but calls it an estimate, not a forecast. The author concludes that capital allocation should weigh the changing size of the problem as much as proposed-solution ingenuity (about 200 words).
items.title: Assumptions in Energy-Transition Forecasts Shape Demand and Investment

items.summary: Counterpoint Research reports July–September 2026 Indian smartphone shipments fell 20% annually, with budget phones under ₹20,000 down 47%. Samsung became number one after nine quarters on 17% share. Rising memory chip costs may push prices higher post-festival season.
items.title: Samsung Regains India Smartphone Sales Lead Amid Budget Phone Slump

items.summary: Cybersecurity firm Kaspersky has warned consumers about fraudulent websites offering fake deals on Apple's newly launched iPhone Duo, cautioning buyers against attractive discounts, suspicious pre-orders and requests for personal information. According to Kaspersky, the iPhone Duo officially went on sale on October 23, 2026, marking Apple's entry into the foldable smartphone market. The launch has created an opportunity for cybercriminals to exploit consumer excitement and target customers looking for early access to the premium device.
items.title: Kaspersky Warns of iPhone Duo Scam Websites

items.summary: The author proposes that cybercriminals are not the organized geniuses often imagined, but a lower-skill demographic. Modeling estimated around 720,000 people in the online criminal economy, with roughly 90% working in scam and fraud call-center operations. The piece suggests these groups operate from middle- and lower-income countries where hiring is cheaper.
items.title: Author's Theory on Why Cybercrime Losses Stay Low

items.summary: A banking lobby group, UK Finance, has been accused of cherrypicking data and misleading the British government by claiming a bank tax rise at next week's budget would leave London less competitive than rival hubs. Its PwC-computed report lists London as most tax-intensive at 46.2%, ahead of Amsterdam (42.2%), Frankfurt (39.1%), Dublin (29%) and New York (27.9%). Campaigners question why Paris is excluded, though UK Finance says it could not produce a robust like-for-like figure. Guardian calculations reviewed by an accountancy firm put the same bank in Paris at 51.6% to 57.3%, up to 11.1 percentage points higher than London. TUC's Paul Nowak called it misleading; Positive Money's Simon Youel questioned whether Paris was cynically omitted. Barclays' boss said a tax hit would be bearable, while JP Morgan's Jamie Dimon warned of scrapping a new £3bn London headquarters if Britain turned hostile to banks.
items.title: Banks' tax-rankings group accused of hiding Paris

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey meets weekly with Prime Minister Keir Starmer (Andy Burnham) at Downing Street for curry dinners to work through the politics behind next week's budget. Aides say these informal sessions help him develop ideas beyond cautious Treasury briefings, though some colleagues worry about reconciling his approach with Labour's economic record and note early tensions in their partnership. Healey aims to give consumers 'breathing space' as he drafts a low-key statement on 28 October amid rising costs linked to the Iran war, higher interest rates and inflation expected above 4%. Analysts warn voters may not feel grateful if support measures stay modest.
items.title: Healey's curry nights and advisers ahead of Labour budget

items.summary: The World Development Report 2026, titled 'The Promise of Artificial Intelligence,' argues that many low-income countries face a deficit in the human skills needed to build economic growth. The report suggests new AI tools can broaden access to skills and improve service delivery where it is thin—for example, noting an experiment with AI advisors in Ethiopia increased wheat yields 38%. It also observes that lower-income economies are unlikely to lead in frontier AI or advanced chips but may gain most from greater knowledge access. The WDR acknowledges practical issues: possible job displacement at call centers and the need for complementary infrastructure investments.
items.title: World Bank Report Frames AI as Tool for Low-Income Countries

items.summary: Jordan Bardella was overwhelmingly re-elected leader of France's National Rally, securing 98.98% of the vote in an uncontested election and receiving 75,497 votes according to election overseer Yoann Gillet. The result positions Bardella as a potential prime minister while Marine Le Pen prepares her presidential campaign ahead of the 2027 election. A counter-demonstration drew around 11,000 protesters per authorities estimates.
items.title: Bardella re-elected as RN prepares Le Pen for presidential bid amid protests

items.summary: Floods in Argentina's northeastern provinces killed two people and displaced more than 2,000 others as river levels rose during the El Nino season. Heavy rainfall lifted the Parana, Uruguay and Iguazu rivers near Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay borders. In Chaco province between 1,200 and 1,300 residents left home; Corrientes saw over 1,000 displaced after an embankment broke in Paso de la Patria, where two workers drowned. Misiones lost more than 100 homes. Authorities warned of further rises next week.
items.title: Argentina Floods Kill Two, Displace Thousands Amid El Nino

items.summary: Hurricane Vance remained a Category 2 storm in the Pacific Ocean, positioned 615 kilometers (382 miles) south-southwest of Acapulco according to Mexico’s National Meteorological Service on October 24. The agency reported its location while monitoring intensity and movement across the eastern Pacific. Officials noted the storm’s distance and trajectory affect risks to coastal communities in southern and western Mexico, where Category 2 winds reach up to 177 kilometers per hour and heavy rainfall may trigger flash floods or landslides.
items.title: Mexico’s Meteorological Service Tracks Hurricane Vance as Category 2

items.summary: The Euronews newsroom presents its October 24, 2026 evening bulletin as a quick roundup of the day's most important stories across Europe and beyond. The outlet frames itself around independence and a European perspective, offering viewers an overview spanning world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel with context for a fast-moving day.
items.title: Euronews Evening News Bulletin Promises a Fast Overview of Global Stories

items.summary: On October 24, RB Leipzig beat promoted Elversberg 4-0 in the Bundesliga, with Romulo Cardoso scoring twice and Tidiam Gomis and Christoph Baumgartner also finding the net. The result lifted Leipzig to fifth place after they had won all four home games this season. Elsewhere, Rayan Philippe scored a late winner as Paderborn beat Hamburg 1-0.
items.title: RB Leipzig dominate Elversberg as Philippe scores late winner for Paderborn

items.summary: Police arrested a 33-year-old male suspect after fire engulfed Adolf Hitler's Alpine retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus or Eagle's Nest, on Friday night above Berchtesgaden. Local media reported that the site had been largely destroyed and urged the public to avoid the area. The residence was one of several buildings used by the Nazi dictator during World War Two.
items.title: Fire Engulfs Hitler's Eagle's Nest Retreat

items.summary: The Ukrainian government announced that Ukraine has a “stable connection to Starlink” ten days after the satellite system was suddenly restricted, capping terminal speeds at 160km/h (99mph). The limits hampered drone interception and cancelled strikes. Blame is disputed: Zelenskyy called it a planned US operation, while Trump blamed Musk’s SpaceX, Rubio denied presidential involvement, and Vance backed Musk.
items.title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink link stable after restrictions

items.summary: Sam Fender responded to fan criticism over high ticket prices for his 2027 stadium tour by promising on Instagram that they “are getting changed.” He said he was “not happy with these prices” and added the cost had been inflated more than intended. The £130.75 front standing price drew particular backlash, though tickets at other venues also exceeded £100.
items.title: Sam Fender Promises Lower Ticket Prices for Proper Massive Tour

items.summary: On International Gibbon Day, Mongabay shared stories of threats and protection facing Asia's gibbons. In the first eight months of 2025, gibbon trafficking seizures reached an all-time high: 336 individuals were recorded between January and August alone. Many babies die in capture or transport; one support officer said only about one in ten reaches a buyer, with traffickers losing roughly 80-90% of them. In response, local women on Java are learning gibbon conservation through textile-printing inspired by the animals.
items.title: Gibbon Trafficking Hits Record High as Communities Turn Guardians

items.summary: A cybersecurity incident involving unauthorised access to Alliance Medinet's membership database compromised the personal data of about 110,000 members. Parent company Alliance Healthcare Group said in a filing that names, identification numbers and contact information were exposed, with bank details and one medical diagnosis possibly affected. Insurers HSBC Life, Income Insurance and Singlife reported smaller affected groups and stressed no evidence their own systems or health records were breached; investigations remain ongoing.
items.title: Alliance Medinet Cyber Incident Exposes Personal Data of Insured Members

items.summary: Vanessa Trump, former wife of Donald Trump Jr and mother of five with President Donald Trump's eldest son, announced she is cancer-free six months after her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year. In a video posted on Friday through her daughter Kai's Instagram account, she said test results 'came back clear.' The pair plan to discuss awareness and prevention next week. According to the American Cancer Society, about 1 in 8 US women develop breast cancer.
items.title: Vanessa Trump Announces She Is Cancer-Free After Breast Diagnosis

items.summary: Michel Martelly, Haiti's former president and musician known as 'Sweet Micky,' registered his candidacy Friday under the Debloke coalition banner. The presidential election is scheduled for December 13, the first general elections in more than 10 years. Observers question whether voting will proceed given gang violence that has displaced over 1.4 million people and controls roughly 70 percent of Port-au-Prince.
items.title: Haiti's Ex-President Martelly Registers for Upcoming Elections Amid Gang Violence Concerns

items.summary: On Tuesday Libya's eastern parliament unanimously approved a maritime agreement with Turkey creating a direct economic corridor between the two countries. The accord disregards Greek islands and clashes with claims by Athens of an exclusive economic zone around them. On X, Turkey's Foreign Ministry said Greece firmly rejects the deal with European Union backing; EU high representative Kaja Kallas added that it infringes on third states' rights. Analysts warn tensions could escalate as extraction begins and threaten the EastMed pipeline project. The dispute centers on how islands earn maritime zones under international law.
items.title: Libya's Parliament Backs a Turkey Maritime Deal, Straining Ties With Greece

items.summary:
The United States approved lenacapavir, the world's only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV, as a first step toward global rollout. In Mbarara, western Uganda — where the 10% HIV rate is double the national average and infection trends are linked to sex work in urban hot spots like Kijungu — the drug is scarce. Only thousands of doses remain after being rationed across remote districts including Lira and Mbarara, so people there often receive cabotegravir instead. Local counsellors say funding cuts have ended community outreach services that once delivered prevention closer to communities. The US and Global Fund aim to purchase lenacapavir for up to 3 million people by the end of 2028; by mid-September, 430,000 doses had been delivered globally, with national programs reporting more than 118,000 people receiving it.

visual null},
items.title: Uganda's HIV Prevention Injection Faces Dose Shortages in Mbarara

items.summary: Donna Nelson, a former Greens candidate and Aboriginal health advocate convicted of drug smuggling after being duped in a love scam, has returned to Perth under an international prison transfer. Her daughters Ashlee Charles and Kristal Hilaire say the arrangement lifted a weight off their lives. Nelson was arrested at Narita International Airport in January 2023 and sentenced to six years; she is now held at Bandyup Women's Prison. The family hopes for parole in February.
items.title: Daughters rejoice as Donna Nelson returns from Japan

items.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in Dandong, China on Saturday via the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge, according to Seoul. He met Chinese Premier Li Qiang a day before the anniversary marking Chinese troops' entry into the 1950-1953 conflict. This was his sixth visit to China.
items.title: Kim Jong Un Visits China Ahead of Korean War Anniversary

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and other senior members of the ruling party will gather in Beijing on Monday for a plenary session that may signal China's next generation of leadership. The fifth Central Committee meeting precedes next year's five-yearly congress, where Xi is expected to win a fourth term.
items.title: Xi Jinping and top Communist Party leaders meet for Fifth Plenum

items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged a large-scale military operation in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers and wounded three at an Israeli checkpoint near Hebron. The Israeli military is demolishing homes and forcibly removing hundreds of Palestinians from the neighborhood, which Human Rights Watch called war crimes. Analysts link the response to Netanyahu's October 27 election campaign.
items.title: Netanyahu Pledges Large-Scale West Bank Operation After Checkpoint Attack

items.summary: In Bosnia and Herzegovina, children with cognitive disabilities often face digital isolation because caregivers prioritize limiting internet use over teaching safe navigation. The country has approximately 550-700 such children, supported by three specialized associations that lack accessible online-safety tools. A group of IT professionals developed SafeClick (Siguran klik), a video game using simple stories and pictures to help young people practice responding to suspicious messages, meeting strangers, or facing cyberbullying without punishment for mistakes. The playable version awaits approval from the App Store and Google Play.
items.title: Bosnian Developers Create Video Game for Children With Down Syndrome

items.summary: Aditya Thackeray, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and MLA, wrote to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday seeking a stay on the proposed Amazon data centre until an expert committee submits its report. The 17-member Kakodkar-led committee was constituted almost 10 days ago amid health and environmental concerns as Maharashtra pushes to become India's leading data centre hub.
items.title: Shiv Sena MLA Opposes Amazon Data Centre in Thane

items.summary: BJP MLA Ritesh Tiwari attacked veteran actor Naseeruddin Shah over his support for students protesting at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute in Kolkata. Tiwari, citing family lineage, called Shah an opponent of the BJP and Sangh. His remarks followed Shah's criticism of the West Bengal government after reports that students faced show-cause notices and surveillance.
items.title: BJP MLA Ritesh Tiwari Attacks Naseeruddin Shah Over SRFTI Row

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) strongly criticised National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah for claiming Pakistan was “protecting” Jammu and Kashmir residents by repeatedly raising the Kashmir issue internationally. BJP leaders, including Ravinder Raina, Suresh Kumar Khanna, Altaf Thakur, Vijay Sharma, G M Shaheen and Vinod Bansal, condemned his remarks as an act of treason and anti-country behaviour, alleging he echoed Pakistan's narrative despite holding constitutional positions. Congress also disagreed with Abdullah but raised concerns about the delay in restoring statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.
items.title: BJP Slams Farooq Abdullah Over Kashmir-Pakistan Claim

items.summary: AU Small Finance Bank reported a 53% profit jump in the second quarter, with pre-provision operating profit rising 28% to Rs 1,514 crore from Rs 1,210 crore. Net interest income climbed 32% to Rs 2,820 crore while net interest margin reached 5.8%. The bank, now India's largest small finance bank and transforming into a universal lender, also saw provisions fall 25% to Rs 359 crore.
items.title: AU Small Finance Bank Reports Strong Q2 Profit Growth

items.summary: Thousands protested in Istanbul and Ankara on Saturday over growing government pressure on independent Turkish media, including arrests, censorship and outlet takeovers, as reported by AFP. Police estimated around 3,000 attended the Ankara demonstration. The protests come amid concerns over restrictions since a 2016 coup attempt; the Turkish Journalists' Union says authorities jailed 11 journalists in two months.
items.title: 'Can no longer breathe': Thousands protest in Turkey over media crackdown

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration seized about 43.56 tonnes of food products and 719.2 litres of milk and ghee during a statewide enforcement drive, Press Trust of India reported, citing officials. The haul was collectively valued at Rs 1.56 crore and included items suspected to be substandard, adulterated or incorrectly labelled. Separately, the department destroyed 564 litres of milk in Mumbai and suspended licences across divisions including Nashik, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Nagpur after inspections found violations such as unhygienic kitchens and improper storage.
items.title: 43 tonnes food, 719 litres milk: Maharashtra FDA seizes Rs 1.56 crore haul

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar visited Azerbaijan a year after bilateral ties soured over the country's support for Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. Holding talks with Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov, he called them 'very productive' and pointed to trade, energy and the International North-South Transport Corridor as avenues for closer cooperation. According to the Indian Embassy in Baku, bilateral trade reached $401 million in 2025. ONGC Videsh Ltd has invested more than $1.2 billion in Azerbaijani oil fields and a pipeline. Tourism figures show arrivals rising from 4,853 in 2014 to about 166,944 in 2025 after an earlier boycott. Whether the visit translates into a meaningful reset remains uncertain.
items.title: Jaishankar's Baku Visit Aims to Reset India-Azerbaijan Ties

items.summary: An India Today investigation on Postmortem examines how the Lawrence Bishnoi criminal network tracked actor Tiger Shroff after a daylight shooting targeting him in Mumbai's Juhu on October 18, 2026. Shooter Anil Pandit claimed responsibility and issued warnings against those collaborating with Salman Khan. Police arrested three young shooters from Kota, Rajasthan, plus logistics suppliers from Delhi and Haryana.
items.title: Bishnoi Gang Plotting to Shoot Tiger Shroff in Mumbai

items.summary: Former Indian batter Ajinkya Rahane named an all-time India Test XI limited to players he played alongside, naming MS Dhoni as captain. He chose Murali Vijay and Shikhar Dhawan as openers with Rahul Dravid at No. 3 and Sachin Tendulkar at No. 4. Kohli and Rohit Sharma were left out. Rahane retired in July this year after scoring eight runs in his final innings, finishing Tests with 5,077 runs from 85 matches at an average of 38.46.
items.title: Rahane's India Test XI Excludes Kohli and Rohit

items.summary: The Telangana Private Junior College Management Association (TPJMA) alleges that the Telangana Board of Intermediate Education (TGBIE) targeted small private junior colleges with penalties, zero-admission orders, and affiliation cancellations affecting 27 colleges in Hyderabad, Rangareddy and Medchal districts. TGBIE denied the claims as baseless, citing regulatory compliance and student safety measures including fake fire NOC findings across 65 colleges. The board stated no admitted students would be affected while 3,241 junior colleges received admissions statewide this year.
items.title: TPJMA Accuses TGBIE of Harassing Junior Colleges Over Penalties and Zero Admissions

items.summary: Parents of an RG Kar rape-murder victim questioned bail granted on October 17 to former hospital principal Sandip Ghosh, who faces charges over financial irregularities and merit manipulation. The victim's father said he should have received a life sentence; her mother, BJP MLA Ratna Debnath, demanded arrests of those present with her daughter before death and alleged evidence destruction by officials including NS Nigam. Citizen groups Voice of Abhaya and Voice of Women announced a November 12 march on the CBI office demanding accountability.
items.title: RG Kar victim's parents challenge bail and plan protest

items.summary: A 35-year-old man, Shakti Singh alias Bhoora, died after assailants allegedly thrashed him and chopped off his right hand at the wrist near a grocery shop in Ludhiana on Saturday morning. The accused reportedly handed the severed hand to the grocer before fleeing when he refused delivery. One of seven suspects has been arrested; police suspect an old rivalry but say the motive is yet to be established.
items.title: Man beaten and hand severed in Ludhiana; cops suspect old rivalry

items.summary: A woman in Ludhiana, Punjab alleges her in-laws pressured her to convert to Christianity and harassed her over dowry after she married Karanveer Singh Siddhu through Hindu rituals. She says the footage shows a man asking about belief in Jesus Christ before baptizing her in a swimming pool. The circumstances have not been independently verified.
items.title: Ludhiana Woman Alleges Forced Conversion and Dowry Harassment by In-Laws

items.summary: Mumbai reported two separate road accidents that killed two people within hours, raising concerns about road safety and negligent driving. In Vikhroli West, a 23-year-old motorcyclist was declared dead after their vehicle crashed into a dumper allegedly parked without warning signals or barricades; his friend sustained serious injuries. Separately in Kurla East, an 84-year-old man died when a car reportedly ran over him while he slept beside a road divider. Police registered cases and launched investigations under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Motor Vehicles Act against both drivers, with further inquiries underway.
items.title: Two Road Accidents in Mumbai Claim Two Lives Within Hours

items.summary: Anilkumar Bolla, a 29-year-old Indian technology professional based in Abu Dhabi, won the largest lottery prize ever awarded in the UAE—100 million dirham (approximately ₹240 crore)—in October 2025. A year later, he says spending time with his family has become his top priority and describes winning as transformative.
items.title: UAE Lottery Winner Anilkumar Bolla Reflects on Windfall a Year Later

items.summary: In India's mutual fund industry, some of the smallest asset managers are delivering better returns than its largest schemes across several equity categories. A portfolio performance comparison found that active equity schemes from newer asset management companies launched in 2023 or later beat the three largest established schemes over one year, where data was available. The analysis covered 24 schemes across eight newcomers and all eight fund categories. Small-cap funds led the outperformance; large-cap gaps were narrower. One younger scheme still lost money. The article notes the window is short and differences in sector exposure may explain results, so it remains too early to draw firm conclusions. Published October 24, 2026.
items.title: India's New Mutual Funds Outperform Established Giants

items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate filed a plea before the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi High Court's May 29 order that quashed its enforcement case information report in the NewsClick money laundering matter. The ED argued the high court ignored the case and delayed judgment by five months, though the matter remains unlisted.
items.title: ED seeks Supreme Court review of NewsClick PMLA quashing

items.summary: As Brazilians head into a second-round presidential vote on October 25, the article frames Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s Brazil as one of few regional leaders resisting Donald Trump. Author Dawisson Belém Lopes argues that challenger Flávio Bolsonaro leans toward “peripheral realism,” accepting subordinate status to powerful nations and joining initiatives like the Shield of the Americas. Citing economists Laura Carvalho and Joseph Stiglitz, he warns a Bolsonaro win could trigger recession if public spending is cut by as much as 1.5% of GDP. The piece notes Brazil’s role as a supplier of water and rare earths for AI development, suggesting continued extractive dependence under any Trump-aligned government.
items.title: Brazil's Election Seen as a Trump-Alignment Test for Latin America

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department says a low-pressure area over the central and southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to strengthen on October 25 and become a cyclonic storm by Monday morning. IMD forecasts heavy rainfall across parts of Tamil Nadu, including Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai, Nagapattinam, Tiruvarur and Thanjavur, with very heavy rain in several areas on October 28 as the system approaches near the Andhra Pradesh coast. Coastal states have been put on alert.
items.title: IMD Warns of Developing Cyclone Over Bay of Bengal

items.summary: In Andhra Pradesh, Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu accused the Jagan Mohan Reddy-led YSRCP of disrupting local bodies polls through violence and criminal politics. The YSRCP countered that the ruling TDP government was undermining democracy via alleged collusion with police and the State Election Commission. Both sides traded allegations as nominations closed.
items.title: Andhra bypoll nominations disrupted amid YSRCP-TDP clash

items.summary: Jenni Ramone, an associate professor at Nottingham Trent University, reviews Barbara Kingsolver's new novel Partita through the lens of its title form. The protagonist Livia is 20 years old and studying piano on scholarship in the United States before her brother dies by suicide when he was 18; that grief shapes decades of her life. Chapters are named for musical movements and alternate between adolescence, early adulthood, and a present-day scene in which Livia clears out her late mother's hoarded home. The review argues art helps people understand themselves and heal rather than merely reflecting reality, noting the book has received rave reviews as a character study of women across generations.
items.title: A musician's life as a musical partita

items.summary: Mumbai police arrested Pranjal Thakran (22) in Indore on Saturday for his alleged role in the October 18 attack on actor Tiger Shroff's car. Police sources said two men fired shots at the vehicle before fleeing; the actor escaped unhurt while a driver and bystander were injured. Mumbai police separately recovered two firearms from Surat, which officials say may have been used against the actor.
items.title: Police arrest suspect in Tiger Shroff shooting attempt, recover firearms from Surat

items.summary: BJP leaders criticized National Conference leader Farooq Abdullah after he suggested that Pakistan's international campaign on Kashmir was pressuring India. Sat Sharma, Arjun Munda, Amar Kumar Bauri and Deepak Prakash condemned the remarks, defending Centre policies following the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A. The row reflects ongoing political differences over Kashmir's status and Pakistan's involvement in the dispute. (With inputs from ANI).
items.title: BJP Leaders Slam Farooq Abdullah Over Kashmir Remarks and Pakistan's Role

items.summary: On 23 October, Muslims prayed at the century-old Race Course mosque in Delhi after receiving an eviction notice from the Land and Development Office on 19 October demanding vacating within six days. Worshippers feared it could be their last prayer there, with claims of possible demolition. The Waqf Board declared the site a heritage property and launched a probe. Nearby residents, whose homes were demolished in Bhai Ram Camp, Masjid Camp and DID Camp, received rehabilitation flats 50 km away at Savda Ghevra, though many remain dissatisfied.
items.title: Delhi mosque faces demolition amid eviction notice and prayers
